review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner (self-review, not independent approval)
review.decision: Preserve exact frontend authentication while separating transient observation gaps and diagnosing bounded startup admission
review.notes: User authorized diagnostics/startup readiness; no real restore or live input. A local frontend handshake currently coalesces missing process/TTY evidence and hard mismatches into 403 without diagnostic reason. Admit only kernel peer tied to this controlled child launch, stable pane/root/client birth and foreground TTY. Wait for cmd.Start identity publication before evaluating an early connection. Use a single 4s admission context, at most 4 attempts and cancellable pauses only for unavailable observations; peer/home/pane/TTY/birth/ambiguity conflicts refuse without retry. Inspect direct child launches with two snapshots of exact pane/bridge/client PIDs; generic launchers retain full ancestry resolution and ambiguity protection. Reuse the existing terminal verifier and legacy Resolve contract, preserve excluded/native modes and no relaunch/fallback after child starts. Emit value-free stage/cause/attempt/timing diagnostics and an actionable local error without prompt/argv/credentials. Record old-red/new-green using isolated deterministic inspector/gate seams; no production daemon, user thread, permissions or installed services. Runtime/real reboot acceptance is separate. Planned source changes may add context-aware inspection and ReadAgent while legacy wrappers retain budgets.

cases.description: Terminal readiness observations retain strict identity and use a bounded exact-launch fast path
cases.setup: Synthetic before/after process records, actual inspector/findClient logic, controlled stdin/pane reads and direct/native versus generic launcher ancestry
cases.action: Resolve valid direct and wrapped clients; vary absent snapshots/stdin, foreground/TTY/peer/birth changes, ambiguous branches and pane metadata; inspect exact PID selection and parent-context cancellation
cases.expected: Only stable unique foreground Codex with verified stdin and exact launch ancestry is accepted. Missing reads classify transient; explicit conflicts classify hard refusal. Direct child snapshots are scoped to pane/bridge/client; generic ancestry keeps existing protections. Cancellation does not extend the parent deadline; legacy Resolve behavior is unchanged. No real process or terminal mutation.

cases.description: Frontend admission reports typed causes and binds only the controlled launch
cases.setup: Actual Begin frontend function with isolated HOME/CODEX_HOME, injected current pane/client observation and process incarnation readers
cases.action: Admit exact launch; vary peer versus client, launch ancestry, backend command/birth availability, invalid request, pane disappearance and canceled inspection; compare persistent files before/after
cases.expected: Known peer/launch mismatch, invalid identity and changed pane cannot acquire authority; transient unreadable evidence is distinguishable from mismatch. No thread discovery/resume/input or persisted binding occurs during admission. Legacy Begin API and current binding/freshness checks remain valid.

cases.description: Bridge waits for launch publication and retries only transient admission within one deadline
cases.setup: Actual readiness/admission driver, controlled attempt and wait functions, real cancellation channels with deterministic ordering and synthetic typed errors
cases.action: Deliver an early request before launch publication, then open the gate; exercise transient-then-ready, mismatch, exhausted attempts, deadline/cancel and launch failure; inspect HTTP/status reason and diagnostic fields
cases.expected: No check executes before publication; successful transient retry authorizes exactly once. Hard refusal runs once, no second child or native fallback, failures preserve specific nonsecret reason and retry eligibility. All attempts share a 4s parent budget and at most four checks; canceled/deadline work cannot later authorize. Old immediate refusal fails the transient/early-publication expectations; cancellation does not require a timing-race sleep.
